titulo: Práctica de Inglés — Repaso completo (Quiz #1: The Mariana Trench, gramática y vocabulario)

temas.explicacion:
Definitions from the book:
  • trench — A trench is a long, narrow groove or ditch.
  • summit — The summit of a mountain is its top or highest point.
  • thrive — When living things thrive, they grow well and are healthy.
  • prehistoric — Something that is prehistoric is very old, from a time before history was recorded.
  • vital — If something is vital, it is needed or very important.
  • glimpse — A glimpse is a very quick look at something.
  • submersible — If something is submersible, it can go or work under water.
  • remotely — If you use something remotely, you control it from a distance.
  • autonomous — If something is autonomous, it controls itself.
temas.microleccion: Ejemplo con otra palabra (no es una de la lista): la palabra extinct aparece en la oración 'Scientists say the giant shark called Megalodon is extinct — none are alive today.' Para entender su significado, me fijo en las pistas del contexto: dice que 'ninguno está vivo hoy'. Eso me dice que extinct significa que un tipo de ser vivo ya no existe en ningún lugar de la Tierra. Así se usan las pistas de contexto para descubrir el significado de una palabra nueva, igual que con las 9 palabras de esta práctica.

temas.explicacion: Texto literal del libro (Into Reading, 'Marvels of Nature: The Mariana Trench'): 'Many people know that the highest point on Earth is at the top of Mount Everest. That famous peak towers 29,035 feet (8,850 m) above sea level. It is in the Himalaya Mountains, near the border of China and Nepal. But how many people can name the lowest place in the world? That point is at the bottom of the Mariana Trench, a valley in the floor of the Pacific Ocean. The trench lies just east of the Mariana Islands, southeast of China and Japan.' 'Inside that groove in the ocean floor is the Challenger Deep, the deepest spot in the world. It lies 210 miles (338 km) from the island of Guam. It is about 36,000 feet (11,000 m) below sea level—almost 7 miles (11 km) deep. If Mount Everest were placed in the Challenger Deep, the mountain's peak would still be under 7,000 feet (2,134 m) of water.' 'But no human, not even an expert diver, could survive the environment of the Challenger Deep. In this pitch-black world, the temperature is about 36°F (2°C). The human body shuts down quickly in water that cold. A person on the ocean floor also would be crushed by the weight of the water.' 'Anglerfish have bioluminescent, built-in fishing poles... The anglerfish waves it to attract other fish. When a fish approaches, the angler snaps up the prey.' 'The Mariana Trench is so deep because of movement in Earth's surface... At the Mariana Trench, a heavy plate of rock on the ocean floor is pressing against a plate of lighter rock... the heavier ocean plate plunges downward at a steep angle into Earth's mantle.' 'The Mariana Trench was discovered in 1875. Scientists on the British ship HMS Challenger used a machine to measure the ocean depth...' 'In 1951 the British Royal Navy vessel HMS Challenger II returned to the area with a modern measuring device... called echo sounding, or sonar... The deepest point it found was 35,760 feet (10,900 m). That point was named the Challenger Deep, after the ship.' 'People got their first glimpse of the Challenger Deep in 1960. That year scientist Jacques Piccard and U.S. Navy Lieutenant Don Walsh traveled to the bottom. They rode in the Trieste, a submersible vehicle... It was 35,813 feet (10,916 m) below the surface.' 'After this exploration, there were only two unmanned submarines that visited the Challenger Deep until March 25, 2012. That was when filmmaker James Cameron reached the bottom in the Deepsea Challenger.' 'In May 2019, businessman Victor Vescovo reached the bottom of the Challenger Deep in a submarine called DSV Limiting Factor.' 'Navy submarines patrolling the world's oceans like to stay in deep water. It is more difficult for enemies to detect them there... the Mariana Trench Marine National Monument was established [in 2009]. It protects the Mariana Islands, the Trench, and the underwater volcanoes.'
temas.microleccion: Ejemplo con otro dato del texto (no es una de las preguntas): el texto dice 'The trench averages about 45 miles (72 km) wide. Para responder una pregunta como '¿cuánto mide de ancho la fosa?', busco la oración exacta del texto que tiene ese dato: 'about 45 miles (72 km) wide' — esa es la respuesta, tomada directamente de lo que dice el libro, no inventada.

temas.explicacion:
Regla general de sustantivos posesivos:
  • Sustantivo singular: agregá 's (an apostrophe + s). Ej.: the book of my brother → my brother's book.
  • Sustantivo plural regular que YA termina en -s: agregá solo un apóstrofe ('), sin otra s. Ej.: the nuts of the squirrels → the squirrels' nuts.
  • Sustantivo plural irregular que NO termina en -s (como women, children, men): agregá 's, igual que un singular. Ej.: the purses of the women → the women's purses.
  • Nombres propios (como Michael): agregá 's. Ej.: the lunch of Michael → Michael's lunch.
temas.microleccion: Ejemplo con otros sustantivos (no son los de las variantes): 'the hat of the man' → man es singular, entonces agrego 's: the man's hat. 'the toys of the dogs' → dogs es plural regular que ya termina en -s, entonces agrego solo el apóstrofe: the dogs' toys. 'the shoes of the men' → men es plural irregular (no termina en -s), entonces agrego 's, igual que un singular: the men's shoes.

temas.explicacion:
Del cuadernillo de gramática (literal):
  • A verb tells what the subject does. A verb can include more than one word: a main verb and a helping verb (ej.: can come, has baked, am walking).
  • An action verb tells what the subject does, did, or will do, en pasado, presente o futuro (ej.: Tameka ran. Ali gives. Sarah will drink.).
  • The main verb tells what the subject does or is (ej.: She washes the dog). A helping verb helps the main verb tell about an action or make a statement (ej.: She is washing the dog).
  • Helping verbs como have, has, had, is, am, are, was, were, will muestran tiempo presente, pasado o futuro. Algunos helping verbs como can, may, must NO muestran tiempo.
  • A linking verb no muestra acción: conecta el sujeto con un sustantivo o adjetivo (ej.: My dog is smelly). Suelen ser formas de be (am, is, are, was, were), o también look, seem, appear, become, feel, grow, smell, taste.
temas.microleccion: Ejemplo con otra oración (no es una de las variantes): 'The pizza tastes amazing.' El verbo 'tastes' no muestra una acción física; conecta 'the pizza' con el adjetivo 'amazing'. Por eso es un linking verb. En cambio, en 'They were running fast', 'running' es el main verb (la acción) y 'were' es el helping verb que ayuda a formar el tiempo pasado progresivo.

temas.nombre: Verb Tenses, Agreement, and Irregular Verbs
temas.explicacion:
Del cuadernillo de gramática (literal):
  • A verb in the present tense shows the action is happening now or over and over. A present-tense verb must agree with the subject: for singular third-person subjects, add -s or -es to most verbs (ej.: Teri takes piano lessons). If the subject is I, you, a plural noun, or a plural pronoun, do NOT add -s/-es. Use am, is, are + -ing para la forma progresiva (is walking, are talking).
  • A verb in the past tense shows the action already happened (ej.: hurried). Use was/were + -ing para la forma progresiva del pasado (was hurrying).
  • A verb in the future tense shows action that will happen (ej.: will hurry). Use will be + -ing para la forma progresiva del futuro (will be hurrying).
  • Formas de be: presente am, is, are; pasado was, were; futuro will be. Use am, was, o will be con I; is, was, o will be con sujetos singulares; are, were, o will be con sujetos plurales.
  • Regular past-tense verbs end with -ed (walk/walked). Irregular past-tense verbs do NOT end with -ed (run/ran). Algunos verbos irregulares no cambian del presente al pasado (read/read); otros terminan en -n o -en cuando se usan con un helping verb (have known, have eaten).
temas.microleccion: Ejemplo con otro verbo (no es uno de las variantes): el verbo 'talk'. Presente: 'She talks to her friend' (agrego -s porque 'she' es singular). Presente progresivo: 'She is talking to her friend'. Pasado: 'She talked to her friend' (regular, termina en -ed). Pasado progresivo: 'She was talking to her friend'. Futuro: 'She will talk to her friend'. Futuro progresivo: 'She will be talking to her friend'. Y un verbo irregular distinto: 'eat' → pasado 'ate' (no termina en -ed), y con helping verb: 'have eaten'.
